About

A chemical engineer who builds things that fly.

I study Chemical Engineering at IIT Madras, and most of my engineering happens in hardware labs and on launch sites. I was the only avionics member in Team Abhyuday’s IREC delegation, coordinated the Aero Club through a national competition season, and spent a summer on vision and guidance for autonomous UAV tracking.

I like owning a system end to end: choosing components, laying out the board, writing the firmware, and then finding out on the pad whether the redundancy was worth it. It was — on our IREC flight, the backup channel on my flight computer fired the drogue when the primary charge failed.

Research & technical work

Models, estimators and a paper

Each entry lists the problem, the method, what I did and what came out of it. All three are complete.

LAT Aerospace · Inter IIT

Inter IIT Tech Meet 14.0, IIT Patna · problem statement by LAT Aerospace

Completed
Full write-up →
Problem
LAT Aerospace’s Inter IIT problem asked for fast models of upper-surface-blowing (USB) lift augmentation. I built thick jet-flap interaction models and validated them against high-fidelity CFD.
Method
S1223 geometry→Jet + Coanda model→6-parameter optimisation→CFD comparison→CL vs α sweeps
My role
Sole modeller in a 30-member IIT Madras team
0.5%Error against high-fidelity CFD
~100×Lower compute time than CFD
4.5CL max from coflow-jet analysis
50+Angle-of-attack configurations

Attitude Estimation

IIT Madras · Prof. Aravind Kumar

Completed
Full write-up →
Problem
A 9-DOF attitude estimator in MATLAB that fuses IMU data with a complementary filter and visualises roll, pitch and yaw in a cockpit-style display.
Method
Gyro · 25 Hz LPF→Accel · 5 Hz LPF→Mag · 5 Hz LPF→Complementary filter · 100 Hz→Horizon · 30 fps
My role
Individual course project · highest grade
100 HzFusion rate
30 fpsHorizon and roll-pitch-yaw display
